plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value is irrational (you'd lose money if you win), and bidding significantly below your value risks losing to a slightly higher bid, even if it's below your true value. Since it's round 1 and there's no history, I will bid slightly below my value to test the waters.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction to a slightly higher bid, even if it's still below your value, resulting in a lost opportunity for profit. Any bid above your value risks overpaying. My value is $35, so I will bid $35.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0 and $49, the expected value of the highest of the remaining two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To win with minimal overpayment, I’ll bid slightly above that, but also considering my own value of $6. Bidding too high risks overpaying significantly, while bidding too low risks losing. A bid of $6.1 is reasonable.
